sections.html:
Derby is a city in Sedgwick County and the largest suburb of Wichita, lying south of the city next to McConnell Air Force Base. The 2020 census counted 25,625 residents and the July 2025 estimate is 26,606. The city covers about 9.6 square miles. Aircraft manufacturing, the base and the school district anchor the local economy, and Textron Aviation, Derby Public Schools and McConnell are the best known employers.

McConnell is a significant hub for the Air Force, so some sellers are households with orders to move on a set date. A listing that needs months to sell may not fit that schedule.

Derby parcels are valued by the county, not by the city, and the city issues permits. Keeping those two straight saves time.

Derby Public Schools, USD 260, serves Derby, McConnell Air Force Base, the Oaklawn Improvement District and some southern parts of Wichita. A Wichita mailing address therefore does not guarantee Wichita schools. The district runs a sixth grade center, a middle school, a high school and an alternative high school in addition to its elementary schools. Wineteer Elementary is the school for McConnell family housing.

Neighboring districts include Haysville USD 261, Mulvane USD 263, Goddard USD 265 and Andover USD 385, which matters if your house is near a boundary. Confirm the district for your own address before you describe the schools to a buyer.

The City of Derby requires permits for many projects, and contractors need a city license. Work that typically needs a permit includes:

  • Fences, decks, garages, pools, sheds, pergolas, gazebos and outdoor kitchens.
  • Most electrical, plumbing and heating or air conditioning work.
  • Driveway approaches, retaining walls, sprinkler systems and wells.
  • Roofing and siding replacement over 400 square feet.
  • Anything built in a flood plain, which also needs a Flood Plain Development Permit.

Inspections catch problems such as an improperly installed water heater, faulty wiring or a deck built below code. To find out whether a contractor holds a city license, call 788-6632 or email permits@derbyweb.com. Inspections must be requested 24 hours ahead on the residential permit form.

If a past owner finished a basement or added a deck without a permit, a buyer's inspector may ask about it. Pulling records from the city before you list can save a deal from stalling.

sections.h2: How does a house sale in Derby work?
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell on your own or take a cash offer. A listing usually involves repairs, showings and a buyer's lender, while a cash buyer can skip the loan step.

In Kansas the deed is the transfer document. It is filed with the Register of Deeds along with a Real Estate Sales Validation Questionnaire, and the County Clerk then updates the tax record. The Sedgwick County Treasurer bills the tax on a Derby parcel, with payment due December 20 for the full amount or first half and May 10 for the second half.

  • Ask the Treasurer for the current balance before you set a closing date.
  • Check for special assessments with the City of Derby or the County Clerk.
  • Gather permit records for any work done on the house.

Derby has hot, humid summers and generally mild to cool winters. Hail and flood risk are matters for a home inspection and your insurer.

Because the city's permit rules include a Flood Plain Development Permit, check whether your lot falls in a mapped flood area before you assume nothing is required. The permit office at 788-6632 can answer questions about flood plain mapping for your address.

The Sedgwick County Appraiser values Derby parcels. Valuation notices go out March 1, and an informal appeal must be returned within 30 days, usually by March 31. A value can be appealed only once per tax year.

If taxes fall behind, the county Treasurer eventually lists parcels that are two and a half or three and a half years delinquent for foreclosure, and a $400 foreclosure fee is added on October 1 of the listing year. Paying in full ends the case, and an owner can redeem up to the close of business the day before the auction.

A cash sale that pays off the balance at closing can resolve the lien. Whoever handles your sale should ask the Treasurer, at 316-660-9000, for an up-to-date payoff before the closing date is set.

sections.h2: What do Derby sellers commonly deal with?
sections.html:
• A short timeline because of a military move or a job change.
  • Unpermitted work that a buyer's inspector flags.
  • Delinquent property tax, which the county Treasurer can pursue through foreclosure after roughly two and a half years.
  • Inherited houses where the family wants a quick sale without staging or repairs.

If one of these fits you, send us the address of your Derby house. We will explain how a cash offer could work and what the closing steps would be.

sections.h2: What to gather before talking to a cash buyer
sections.html:
A short folder of documents speeds things up. None of it is required to ask for an offer, but it answers the buyer's first questions.

  • The deed or a recent tax statement showing the legal owner.
  • Permit records for additions, a new roof, a deck or a finished basement.
  • Any notice from the county about delinquent tax or special assessments.
  • A note on whether the house is occupied by you, a tenant or no one.

With those in hand, the conversation about timing and price is more concrete.

faqs.q: How many people live in Derby, KS?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 25,625 people, and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 26,606.

faqs.q: Which school district covers Derby, Kansas?
faqs.a: Derby Public Schools, USD 260, serves the city, McConnell Air Force Base, the Oaklawn Improvement District and some southern Wichita neighborhoods.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace a roof in Derby?
faqs.a: Roofing and siding replacements over 400 square feet need a permit. Call 788-6632 to confirm for your project.

faqs.q: When is property tax due on a Derby house?
faqs.a: The Sedgwick County Treasurer bills it. Full payment or the first half is due December 20, and the second half is due May 10.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Derby house as-is for cash?
faqs.a: Yes. You can accept a cash offer instead of listing, and the buyer may take the house as it stands. Send us the address and we will explain the steps.
